title: The Left Hand of Darkness
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: A envoy crosses a frozen world where gender is fluid and winter never ends.

title: Piranesi
author: Susanna Clarke
description: A man lives in an infinite house of statues and tides, and keeps its journal.

title: Thinking in Systems
author: Donella Meadows
description: A primer on stocks, flows, feedback loops, and why complex things misbehave.

my.review: The clearest short tour of systems thinking I have read. The leverage-points chapter alone is worth it.

title: The Song of Achilles
author: Madeline Miller
description: Achilles told through the eyes of Patroclus, from boyhood to Troy.

my.review: Devastating in the best way. Drags a little through the war years, then lands everything.

title: Klara and the Sun
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description: An artificial friend observes the human world with unnerving patience.

my.review: Quiet, strange, and warmer than it first appears. Klara's logic stays with you.

title: Babel
author: R. F. Kuang
description: Translation is magic, empire is the price, and Oxford is the machine.

title: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
author: Mark Twain
description: A raft, a river, and the best unreliable narrator in American letters.

title: Gödel, Escher, Bach
author: Douglas Hofstadter
description: Strange loops, fugues, and how self-reference makes minds possible.

my.review: Brilliant, but I bailed at the dialogue about tortoises. Will return with more patience.

title: Circe
author: Madeline Miller
description: The witch of Aiaia tells her own story, gods and all.

title: Braiding Sweetgrass
author: Robin Wall Kimmerer
description: Indigenous wisdom and plant science braid into one way of seeing the land.

my.review: Read it slowly, a chapter a night. It rewires how you notice things.

title: The Martian Chronicles
author: Ray Bradbury
description: Colonists arrive on Mars carrying everything they left behind, including themselves.

title: Ghostwritten
author: David Mitchell
description: Nine narrators, one chain of consequences, spanning the world.
